```{python}
# | label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib as mpl
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

mpl.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans",   # full Cyrillic coverage for figure labels
    "figure.dpi": 150,
    "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False,
    "axes.grid": True,
    "grid.alpha": 0.25,
    "axes.titlesize": 12,
    "axes.titleweight": "bold",
})
sns.set_palette("colorblind")

ACCENT = "#2b6cb0"   # health-supporting / neutral primary
RISK = "#c05621"     # risk factors
MIXED = "#6b7280"

# Locate the repository root, so this report may live at any depth under it.
_root = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents]
             if (p / "pixi.toml").exists())
sys.path.insert(0, str(_root / "src"))
from arkhinfra import paths as P  # noqa: E402

RAW = P.RAW

CATEGORY_EN = {
    "Магазины": "Shops", "Организации": "Organizations",
    "Медицинские организации": "Medical organizations", "Услуги": "Services",
    "Общепит": "Catering", "Образование": "Education",
    "Спортивные объекты": "Sport facilities",
    "Государственные организации": "Government organizations",
    "фастфуд": "Fast food", "Финансовые организации": "Financial organizations",
    "Почта и связь": "Post & communications", "Авто": "Auto", "Культура": "Culture",
    "Досуг и спорт": "Leisure & sport", "Точки продажи табака": "Tobacco outlets",
    "Гостиницы и туризм": "Hotels & tourism",
}
DISTRICT_EN = {
    "Октябрьский округ": "Oktyabrsky", "Округ Майская горка": "Mayskaya Gorka",
    "Соломбальский округ": "Solombalsky", "Округ Варавино-Фактория": "Varavino-Faktoriya",
    "Северный округ": "Severny", "Исакогорский и Цигломенский округа": "Isakogorsky & Tsiglomensky",
    "Ломоносовский округ": "Lomonosovsky", "Маймаксанский округ": "Maymaksansky",
}
VERIF_EN = {
    "only_osm": "OSM only", "only_2gis": "2GIS only",
    "confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm": "OSM + 2GIS (confirmed)",
}

# Rename map from the (Russian) health-export columns to the canonical schema.
HEALTH_RENAME = {
    "Статус проверки": "verification_status", "Источники": "providers",
    "Количество источников": "provider_count", "Категория": "category_orig",
    "Тип": "type_orig", "Организация": "name_orig", "Город": "city_orig",
    "Округ/район": "district_orig", "Адрес": "adress_orig", "Широта": "latitude",
    "Долгота": "longitude", "Сайт": "website_orig", "Телефон": "phone_orig",
    "Часы работы": "opening_hours_orig", "Дата открытия": "opening_date_orig",
    "Тип влияния": "impact", "Полезные группы": "useful_groups",
    "Группы риска": "risk_groups",
}


def load_dataset(which):
    """Return (df, meta) in the canonical schema for either dataset."""
    if which == "health":
        df = pd.read_excel(RAW / "objects_arkhangelsk_2026-06-28_health.xlsx",
                           sheet_name="Объекты").rename(columns=HEALTH_RENAME)
        meta = {"label": "Health & risk subset", "has_impact": True}
    else:
        df = pd.read_csv(RAW / "objects_arkhangelsk_2026-06-28_enriched.csv",
                         sep=";", encoding="utf-8-sig", low_memory=False)
        meta = {"label": "Full enriched export", "has_impact": False}
    for col in ("latitude", "longitude"):
        df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")
    df["provider_count"] = pd.to_numeric(df["provider_count"], errors="coerce")
    df["category_en"] = df["category_orig"].map(CATEGORY_EN).fillna(df["category_orig"])
    df["district_en"] = df["district_orig"].map(DISTRICT_EN).fillna(df["district_orig"])
    df["verif_en"] = df["verification_status"].map(VERIF_EN).fillna(df["verification_status"])
    return df, meta


# ---- Recoding of any object into the 2022 health taxonomy (7 classes) -----
CLASS_2022 = ["Medical", "Sport", "Grocery shops", "Catering",
              "Alcohol shops", "Tobacco outlets", "Industrial"]
ORDER_2022 = CLASS_2022 + ["Other (outside 2022 scheme)"]
# labels used in the 2022 source file -> canonical English class
SRC2022_EN = {
    "Медицинские организации": "Medical", "Спортивные объекты": "Sport",
    "Магазины": "Grocery shops", "Общепит": "Catering",
    "Спецмагазины алкоголя": "Alcohol shops", "Точки продажи табака": "Tobacco outlets",
    "Пром. Объекты": "Industrial",
}
GROCERY_TYPES = {
    "продуктовый магазин", "супермаркет", "гипермаркет", "овощи и фрукты",
    "фрукты-овощи", "булочная", "кулинария", "ярмарка", "рынок",
    "магазин: confectionery", "кондитерская", "мясной магазин",
    "рыбный магазин", "молочный магазин", "магазин у дома",
}


def _has(s, *words):
    m = np.zeros(len(s), dtype=bool)
    for w in words:
        m |= s.str.contains(w, regex=False, na=False)
    return m


def recode_2022(df):
    """Map objects onto the 2022 taxonomy using category + type + name."""
    cat = df["category_orig"].fillna("").astype(str)
    t = df["type_orig"].fillna("").astype(str).str.lower()
    blob = (cat.str.lower() + " | " + t + " | "
            + df["name_orig"].fillna("").astype(str).str.lower())

    tobacco = (cat == "Точки продажи табака") | _has(blob, "табак", "вейп", "сигарет", "кальян", "vape")
    alcohol = _has(t, "алкогол") | _has(blob, "алкомаркет", "винотек") | (_has(t, "винный") & _has(t, "магазин"))
    medical = (cat == "Медицинские организации") | _has(
        blob, "аптек", "поликлин", "больниц", "стоматолог", "клиник", "врач",
        "диагност", "лаборатор", "диспансер", "госпит", "медиц", "оптика",
        "реабилит", "санатор", "профилакт", "роддом", "родильн", "фельдшер")
    sport = (cat == "Спортивные объекты") | _has(
        blob, "спорт", "фитнес", "бассейн", "стадион", "тренаж", "воркаут",
        "каток", "манеж", "йога") | _has(t, "парк", "сквер", "набережн")
    catering = cat.isin(["Общепит", "фастфуд"]) | _has(
        t, "кафе", "фастфуд", "бар", "ресторан", "паб", "кофейн", "столов",
        "закусочн", "пиццери", "суши", "бистро")
    grocery = t.isin(GROCERY_TYPES)
    industrial = _has(blob, "завод", "энергокомплекс", "тэц", "гэс", "фабрика", "промышл", "комбинат")

    return pd.Series(np.select(
        [tobacco, alcohol, medical, sport, catering, grocery, industrial],
        ["Tobacco outlets", "Alcohol shops", "Medical", "Sport", "Catering",
         "Grocery shops", "Industrial"],
        default="Other (outside 2022 scheme)"), index=df.index)


def barh(series, title, xlabel, color=ACCENT, fmt_pct=False, figsize=(7.2, 4.4)):
    s = series.sort_values(ascending=True)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    ax.barh(s.index, s.values, color=color)
    total = s.sum()
    for y, v in enumerate(s.values):
        lbl = f"{v:,} ({v/total*100:.0f}%)" if fmt_pct else f"{v:,}"
        ax.text(v, y, " " + lbl, va="center", ha="left", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xlabel(xlabel); ax.set_title(title)
    ax.margins(x=0.16); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()


df, meta = load_dataset(dataset)
df["category_2022"] = recode_2022(df)

n_obj = len(df)
n_cat = df["category_orig"].nunique()
n_type = df["type_orig"].nunique()
n_dist = df["district_orig"].nunique()
DS_LABEL = meta["label"]
```

# Introduction

This report is the **initial exploratory data analysis (EDA)** of the current
stage of the Northern State Medical University infrastructure project. The
research question — inherited from the 2022 stage (see
[`docs/report_arkhangelsk_2022.md`](../../docs/report_arkhangelsk_2022.md)) — is
**how health-relevant urban infrastructure and health risk factors are
distributed across the districts (*okrugs*) of Arkhangelsk**.

The data is produced by the *ИнфраструктураРФ* program (see
[`docs/infrastructure_rf.md`](../../docs/infrastructure_rf.md)) for Arkhangelsk,
dated **2026-06-28**. This report is parameterised and can be rendered for either
the full city export or the health-and-risk subset.

::: {.callout-note}
## Dataset analysed: **`{python} DS_LABEL`** — `{python} f"{n_obj:,}"` objects
`enriched` = full city inventory · `health` = objects pre-filtered to
health-supporting infrastructure and risk factors. Render the other view with
`pixi run eda-health`.
:::

```{python}
})
```

# Data quality and source verification

Every object carries provenance and verification metadata; confidence is higher
when an object is confirmed by more than one source.

```{python}
# | label: fig-verification
# | fig-cap: "Objects by verification status (data-source confidence)."
vc = df["verif_en"].value_counts()
barh(vc, "Verification status", "Number of objects", fmt_pct=True, figsize=(7.2, 2.9))
```

```{python}
# | label: verif-note
n_multi = int((df["provider_count"] >= 2).sum())
osm_only = int((df["verification_status"] == "only_osm").sum())
```

Only **`{python} f"{n_multi:,}"`** objects
(`{python} f"{n_multi/n_obj*100:.1f}"`%) are confirmed by both OpenStreetMap and
2GIS; the rest come from a single source, and
**`{python} f"{osm_only/n_obj*100:.0f}"`%** rely on OpenStreetMap alone. Absolute
counts are therefore **lower bounds**, consistent with the 2022 finding that
~64% of objects were found in OSM.

```{python}
# | label: fig-completeness

fields = {"Address": "adress_orig", "Opening hours": "opening_hours_orig",
```

Coordinates and addresses are near-complete, so **spatial analysis is reliable**.
Contact details are partial, and *opening date* is essentially absent and should
be dropped from downstream analysis.

# Recoding to the 2022 taxonomy

The 2022 stage used a focused **health-relevant taxonomy of 7 classes**: *Medical
organizations*, *Sport facilities*, *Grocery shops*, *Catering*, *Alcohol shops*,
*Tobacco outlets*, and *Industrial objects*. The current export uses a broader,
generic category system in which, for example, `Магазины` ("Shops") mixes
groceries with clothing, hardware, and alcohol.

To make the two stages comparable, each current object is **recoded into the 2022
taxonomy** (new column `category_2022`) using a transparent rule over
`category_orig`, `type_orig`, and `name_orig` — e.g. pharmacies and clinics →
*Medical*; `Алкогольный магазин` → *Alcohol shops*; hookah lounges → *Tobacco
outlets* (as in 2022); grocery-type shops → *Grocery shops*. Objects that fall
outside the health taxonomy (clothing, services, banks, …) are labelled *Other*.
The complete category/type → class mapping, including everything assigned to
*Other*, is listed in the supplementary table at the end of this report
(@tbl-recode-map).

```{python}
# | label: fig-recode
# | fig-cap: "Current objects recoded into the 2022 taxonomy."
rc = df["category_2022"].value_counts().reindex(ORDER_2022).dropna()
colors = [RISK if c in ("Alcohol shops", "Tobacco outlets") else
          (MIXED if c.startswith("Other") else ACCENT) for c in rc.index]
order = rc.sort_values()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2))
ax.barh(order.index, order.values,
        color=[RISK if c in ("Alcohol shops", "Tobacco outlets") else
               (MIXED if c.startswith("Other") else ACCENT) for c in order.index])
for y, v in enumerate(order.values):
    ax.text(v, y, f" {v:,} ({v/n_obj*100:.0f}%)", va="center", fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("Number of objects"); ax.set_title("Recoded to 2022 taxonomy")
ax.margins(x=0.16); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

in_scheme = int((df["category_2022"] != "Other (outside 2022 scheme)").sum())
```

**`{python} f"{in_scheme:,}"`** objects
(`{python} f"{in_scheme/n_obj*100:.0f}"`%) of the current dataset map into the
2022 health taxonomy; the remainder are outside its scope.

## Comparison with the 2022 classification

```{python}
# | label: tbl-compare
# | tbl-cap: "Class distribution: 2022 stage vs. current dataset (share within the 7-class scheme)."
d22 = pd.read_excel(RAW / "objects_3_districts_2022.xlsx")
c22 = d22["category_orig"].map(SRC2022_EN).value_counts()
cur = df.loc[df["category_2022"] != "Other (outside 2022 scheme)", "category_2022"].value_counts()

cmp = pd.DataFrame(index=CLASS_2022)
cmp["2022 N"] = c22.reindex(CLASS_2022).fillna(0).astype(int)
cmp["2022 %"] = (cmp["2022 N"] / cmp["2022 N"].sum() * 100).round(1)
cmp["Current N"] = cur.reindex(CLASS_2022).fillna(0).astype(int)
cmp["Current %"] = (cmp["Current N"] / cmp["Current N"].sum() * 100).round(1)
tot = pd.DataFrame({"2022 N": [cmp["2022 N"].sum()], "2022 %": [100.0],
                    "Current N": [cmp["Current N"].sum()], "Current %": [100.0]},
                   index=["Total (in scheme)"])
cmp_disp = pd.concat([cmp, tot]).reset_index().rename(columns={"index": "2022 class"})
(cmp_disp.style.hide(axis="index")
 .format({"2022 %": "{:.1f}", "Current %": "{:.1f}"}))
```

The 2022 data covered only three okrugs (1,753 objects) whereas the current
export is city-wide, so the comparison is most meaningful on **shares**. *Grocery
shops*, *Medical*, and *Catering* dominate the health-relevant infrastructure in
both stages; the recoding lets later stages track each class on a like-for-like
basis.

# Spatial and district distribution

All objects are geocoded within the Arkhangelsk bounding box.

```{python}
# | label: fig-map
# | fig-cap: "Spatial distribution of objects, coloured by district (okrug), on an OpenStreetMap/CARTO basemap."
top_d = df["district_en"].value_counts().index.tolist()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 6.0))
for color, d in zip(sns.color_palette("colorblind", len(top_d)), top_d):
    sub = df[df["district_en"] == d]
    ax.scatter(sub["longitude"], sub["latitude"], s=6, alpha=0.5,
               color=color, label=f"{d} ({len(sub):,})")
ax.set_xlabel("Longitude"); ax.set_ylabel("Latitude"); ax.set_title("Objects by district")
ax.set_aspect(1 / np.cos(np.deg2rad(64.55)))
try:
    # Real-map background. Tiles are cached in data/tile_cache, so only the
    # first render needs internet access; offline we keep the plain scatter.
    import contextily as ctx
    tile_cache = RAW.parent / "tile_cache"
    tile_cache.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    ctx.set_cache_dir(str(tile_cache))
    ctx.add_basemap(ax, crs="EPSG:4326", source=ctx.providers.CartoDB.Positron,
                    attribution_size=5)
    ax.grid(visible=False)
except Exception:
    ax.grid(alpha=0.2)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=7, markerscale=2, framealpha=0.9)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: fig-districts

barh(dist, "Objects by district", "Number of objects", fmt_pct=True, figsize=(7.2, 3.8))
```

## Data-quality caveat: district assignment is skewed

**`{python} f"{okt_share:.0f}"`% of all objects are assigned to a single okrug
(Oktyabrsky).** This is inconsistent with the geography of Arkhangelsk and with
the 2022 stage, where Oktyabrsky, Lomonosovsky, and Mayskaya Gorka held
comparable counts. The most likely cause is the automatic okrug-assignment step
of the export. **District-level rates below should be treated as provisional and
the assignment logic re-validated before any substantive spatial conclusions.**



# Frequency of 2022-taxonomy classes by okrug

The core cross-tabulation for the project: **how the recoded health-relevant
classes are distributed across okrugs.** The heatmap is annotated with object

```{python}
# | label: fig-recode-heatmap

sns.heatmap(ct, annot=True, fmt="d", cmap="Blues", linewidths=0.5,
            linecolor="white", cbar_kws={"label": "objects"}, ax=ax)
```

```{python}
# | label: tbl-recode-freq
# | tbl-cap: "Frequency table of recoded 2022-taxonomy classes by district (with totals). \"Other\" = outside the 2022 scheme."
from IPython.display import Markdown

# Districts as rows and short class headers as columns, emitted as a markdown
# pipe table (not Styler HTML) — a 10-district-column table overflows the page.
SHORT_2022 = {"Grocery shops": "Grocery", "Alcohol shops": "Alcohol",
              "Tobacco outlets": "Tobacco", "Other (outside 2022 scheme)": "Other"}
full = pd.crosstab(df["district_en"], df["category_2022"], margins=True, margins_name="All")
keep_cols = [c for c in CLASS_2022 if c in full.columns] + \
            (["Other (outside 2022 scheme)"] if "Other (outside 2022 scheme)" in full.columns else []) + ["All"]
keep_rows = list(df["district_en"].value_counts().index) + ["All"]
full = full.reindex(index=keep_rows, columns=keep_cols).rename(columns=SHORT_2022)
Markdown(full.reset_index().rename(columns={"district_en": "District"})
         .to_markdown(index=False))
```

# Health infrastructure vs. risk factors

```{python}
# | label: healthrisk-compute
t = df["type_orig"].fillna("").astype(str).str.lower()
cat = df["category_orig"].fillna("").astype(str)
blob = (cat.str.lower() + " | " + t + " | " + df["name_orig"].fillna("").str.lower())

health_sub = {
    "Medical": df["category_2022"].eq("Medical"),
    "Sport & recreation": df["category_2022"].eq("Sport"),
}
risk_sub = {
    "Fast food": cat.eq("фастфуд") | _has(t, "фастфуд"),
    "Alcohol": df["category_2022"].eq("Alcohol shops"),
    "Tobacco": df["category_2022"].eq("Tobacco outlets"),
    "Bars / pubs": _has(t, "бар", "паб") & ~_has(t, "барбер"),
    "Hookah / nightlife": _has(blob, "кальян", "ночной клуб", "лаунж"),
}
hr = pd.DataFrame({
    "Group": ["Health-supporting"] * len(health_sub) + ["Risk factor"] * len(risk_sub),
    "Subgroup": list(health_sub) + list(risk_sub),
    "Objects": [int(m.sum()) for m in health_sub.values()] + [int(m.sum()) for m in risk_sub.values()],
})
health_mask = np.logical_or.reduce(list(health_sub.values()))
risk_mask = np.logical_or.reduce(list(risk_sub.values()))
n_health, n_risk = int(health_mask.sum()), int(risk_mask.sum())
```

A transparent heuristic (built on the 2022 recoding plus type keywords) separates
**health-supporting** infrastructure from **risk factors**. Under it the dataset
holds **`{python} f"{n_health:,}"`** health-supporting and
**`{python} f"{n_risk:,}"`** risk-factor objects.

```{python}
# | label: fig-healthrisk
# | fig-cap: "Health-supporting infrastructure (blue) vs. risk factors (orange)."
order = hr.sort_values("Objects")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.8))
ax.barh(order["Subgroup"], order["Objects"],
        color=[ACCENT if g == "Health-supporting" else RISK for g in order["Group"]])
for y, v in enumerate(order["Objects"]):
    ax.text(v, y, f" {v:,}", va="center", fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlabel("Number of objects")
ax.set_title("Health-supporting (blue) vs. risk factors (orange)")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False); ax.margins(x=0.12)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

```{python}
# | label: impact-block
# | output: asis
IMPACT_EN = {"Положительная инфраструктура": "Positive infrastructure",
             "Фактор риска": "Risk factor", "Смешанное влияние": "Mixed"}
USEFUL_EN = {
    "Медицинские организации": "Medical organizations",
    "Аптеки и медицинские товары": "Pharmacies & medical goods",
    "Спортивные объекты": "Sport facilities",
    "Зоны отдыха и прогулок": "Recreation & walking areas",
    "Стоматология и диагностика": "Dentistry & diagnostics",
    "Реабилитация и профилактика": "Rehab & prevention"}
RISK_EN = {
    "Продажа алкоголя": "Alcohol sales",
    "Бары, пабы и ночной досуг": "Bars, pubs & nightlife",
    "Фастфуд и высококалорийный общепит": "Fast food & high-calorie catering",
    "Продажа табака и вейпов": "Tobacco & vape sales",
    "Азартные игры и букмекерские точки": "Gambling & betting"}


def explode_groups(series, mapping):
    s = series.dropna().astype(str).str.split(";").explode().str.strip()
    s = s[s != ""].map(lambda x: mapping.get(x, x))
    return s.value_counts()


if meta["has_impact"]:
    imp = df["impact"].map(IMPACT_EN).fillna(df["impact"]).value_counts()
    ct_imp = pd.crosstab(df["impact"].map(IMPACT_EN).fillna(df["impact"]),
                         df["district_en"])
    order_cols = df["district_en"].value_counts().index
    ct_imp = ct_imp.reindex(columns=[c for c in order_cols if c in ct_imp.columns])

    imp_ord = imp.sort_values()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 2.5))
    ax.barh(imp_ord.index, imp_ord.values,
            color=[RISK if "Risk" in i else (MIXED if "Mixed" in i else ACCENT) for i in imp_ord.index])
    for y, v in enumerate(imp_ord.values):
        ax.text(v, y, f" {v:,}", va="center", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title("Impact type"); ax.set_xlabel("Number of objects")
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False); ax.margins(x=0.16)
    plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

    top6 = df["district_en"].value_counts().index[:6]
    ct6 = ct_imp.reindex(columns=[c for c in top6 if c in ct_imp.columns])
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 2.7))
    sns.heatmap(ct6, annot=True, fmt="d", cmap="Blues", cbar_kws={"label": "objects"},
                linewidths=0.5, linecolor="white", ax=ax)
    ax.set_title("Impact type by okrug"); ax.set_xlabel(""); ax.set_ylabel("")
    plt.xticks(rotation=30, ha="right"); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

    useful = explode_groups(df["useful_groups"], USEFUL_EN)
    risk = explode_groups(df["risk_groups"], RISK_EN)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.6, 3.4))
    u = useful.sort_values(); axes[0].barh(u.index, u.values, color=ACCENT)
    axes[0].set_title("Useful groups"); axes[0].grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    r = risk.sort_values(); axes[1].barh(r.index, r.values, color=RISK)
    axes[1].set_title("Risk groups"); axes[1].grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    for a in axes:
        for y, v in enumerate([p.get_width() for p in a.patches]):
            a.text(v, y, f" {int(v)}", va="center", fontsize=7)
    plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

# Key findings

1. **Scale & scope.** This view (**`{python} DS_LABEL`**) covers
   **`{python} f"{n_obj:,}"` objects** across **`{python} f"{n_cat}"` categories**
   and **`{python} f"{n_type}"` types**.
2. **Source confidence is thin.** Only
   **`{python} f"{n_multi/n_obj*100:.1f}"`%** of objects are multi-source
   confirmed; ~**`{python} f"{osm_only/n_obj*100:.0f}"`%** are OSM-only — counts
   are lower bounds.
3. **Geometry is solid, attributes partial.** Coordinates/addresses are
   near-complete; *opening date* is unusable.
4. **2022 taxonomy recovered.** **`{python} f"{in_scheme/n_obj*100:.0f}"`%** of
   objects recode into the 2022 health scheme, enabling like-for-like comparison
   across stages via `category_2022`.
5. **District assignment is broken.** ~**`{python} f"{okt_share:.0f}"`%** of
   objects fall into one okrug — fix before district-level conclusions.
6. **Health vs. risk is measurable** per okrug (health-to-risk ratio), giving the
   next stage a concrete indicator to map across the city.

## Recommended next steps

- Re-validate the okrug-assignment step of the export (highest priority).
- Review and freeze the `category_2022` recoding rules against the 2022 category
  definitions.
- Enrich source confidence with additional providers (Yandex, 2GIS,
  administrative data) as in the 2022 methodology.
- Once districts are fixed, compute per-district, per-capita accessibility and
  the health-to-risk ratio as the core project output.

# Appendix: dataset dictionary {.appendix}

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `verification_status` | Source confirmation tier (`only_osm`, `only_2gis`, `confirmed_by_2gis_and_osm`) |
| `providers` / `provider_count` | Which sources found the object / how many |
| `category_orig` / `type_orig` | Category and fine-grained type (Russian) |
| `category_2022` | **Derived** — object recoded into the 2022 health taxonomy |
| `name_orig` | Object name |
| `city_orig` / `district_orig` / `adress_orig` | Location text fields |
| `latitude` / `longitude` | Coordinates (WGS84) |
| `website_orig` / `phone_orig` / `opening_hours_orig` / `opening_date_orig` | Contact & schedule |
| `impact` / `useful_groups` / `risk_groups` | Native health classification (health export only) |

# Supplementary: full recoding map to the 2022 taxonomy {.appendix}

The table below lists **every combination of source category, source type and
assigned 2022 class** present in this dataset, with object counts — including
all labels that ended up in *Other (outside 2022 scheme)*. Because the recoding
rules also inspect object names (`name_orig`), a single category/type pair can
split across several 2022 classes (e.g. a tobacco shop typed as a generic shop);
each such split is a separate row. Source types are shown with their original
Russian labels; "—" marks objects with no type recorded.

```{python}
# | label: tbl-recode-map
# | tbl-cap: "Full recoding map: source category + source type → 2022 class, with object counts (all combinations, including Other)."
sup = (df.assign(type_orig=df["type_orig"].fillna("—"),
                 category_orig=df["category_orig"].fillna("—"))
         .groupby(["category_2022", "category_orig", "type_orig"], observed=True)
         .size().rename("Objects").reset_index())
sup["category_2022"] = pd.Categorical(sup["category_2022"], ORDER_2022, ordered=True)
sup = sup.sort_values(["category_2022", "Objects", "type_orig"],
                      ascending=[True, False, True])
sup["category_orig"] = sup["category_orig"].map(CATEGORY_EN).fillna(sup["category_orig"])
sup = sup.rename(columns={"category_2022": "2022 class",
                          "category_orig": "Source category",
                          "type_orig": "Source type (Russian)"})
Markdown(sup.to_markdown(index=False))
```
